Forward Deployed Engineers are the technical tip of the spear at Exa. Partnered with an Account Executive, you own the technical win: you run discovery with customer engineering teams, design solutions on Exa's API, build and deliver demos and POCs that prove value, and turn technical evaluations into closed deals. In this role, you will:

- Own the technical side of the sales cycle: discovery, solution design, demos, POCs/POVs, and technical objection handling, in partnership with your AE

- Run the technical side of expansion: spot new use cases in existing accounts and turn them into evaluations, with your AE

- Build working demos and prototypes on Exa's API tailored to each customer's use case - agents, research, search, enrichment

- Tell the story: translate Exa's capabilities into use-case narratives that land with CTOs, engineers, and PMs alike

- As a founding regional hire, support early customers through onboarding and initial implementation while we build out dedicated post-sales

- Comfort with ambiguity and early-stage intensity: you can run several evaluations in parallel, prioritize what moves deals, and your job description will change as the region grows

- Familiarity with the modern AI stack - LLMs, RAG, agents - and how customers evaluate it; you can scope a POC with clear success criteria

- Based in region with willingness to travel for customer engagements

- Have led engineers and want to move toward the customer, or are an SE who wants to be more hands-on than your last role allowed

- Are genuinely curious about AI and have built things with LLMs - side projects count

- Are energized by being the first: first hire, first deal, first playbook in a region

- Have run enterprise evaluations end-to-end - POC success criteria, security questionnaires, RFP responses

In practice, that means helping brands find the right creators, understand their audiences, evaluate fit, and manage campaigns across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube without drowning in spreadsheets, guesswork, and manual work.
We are looking for a Senior Product Engineer to help us take that product further. We already have a strong team of around 20 engineers across four product teams, and we’re continuing to grow as we take on more ambitious problems.
What you’ll actually do
As a Senior Product Engineer at Modash, you’ll work closely with product and engineers to turn messy customer problems into simple, useful product experiences.

•
Discovery: creator search that makes the product value obvious in the first session.

•
CRM: relationship management and outreach tools that make teams forget about existence of Google Sheets.

•
Campaigns: performance aggregation across millions of pieces of creator content, helping customers see what worked and what to do next.

•
Creator: affiliate management, attribution, and payouts that make Modash the easiest way for brands to pay creators.

Turn customer pain into product decisions. Understand what users are trying to do, where they get stuck, and what the simplest useful solution looks like.

•
Own work from problem to production. Shape the approach, build the solution, ship it, measure what happens, and improve it based on feedback.

•
Work across the stack and make tradeoffs clearly. Move between frontend, backend, infrastructure, data modeling, debugging, and handling product decisions depending on what the problem needs.

Raise the quality of decisions around you. Ask better questions, challenge weak assumptions, give useful feedback, and help the team keep momentum without waiting for perfect certainty.

• You care about product outcomes, not just technical elegance.

• You are comfortable with ambiguity and can create clarity for yourself and others.

• You work well with product designers and care about the quality of the customer experience.

• You care more about technical elegance than customer outcomes.

Bonus points if...

• You have worked with Vue, Node.js, TypeScript, AWS, MongoDB, or ClickHouse.

• You have worked on technically deep product surfaces: complex workflows, integrations, data-heavy systems, automation, or customer-facing infrastructure.
